reviews.comment: Dr. Turkan is a good professor, she cares a lot about the students success which to some people is annoying. She is truly more there for the students than the material, so yes you might be forced to learn a lot on your own but guess what it's college... I'd rather have a prof who cares and gives As than one who teaches and fails the entire class.

Dr Turkan herself is pretty ok, she cares a lot about the students and clearly wants you to succeed.The class itself is ass though, which isn't her fault. It's way too much work for a 1 credit hour class and the topics jump around randomly with lots of group work and a term project that isn't explained super well. Lots of extra credit though.

Most of the issues with this class mostly  come from the department and not Turkan. However her accent can get a lil annoying, those “T” and “P” syllables can begin to sound like gunshots which is a little worrying and very annoying. She's alright I guess.

This class only exists to crowd your week with work. Lecture is disconnected, shifting from sigfigs to phys to Excel with no direction, making studying a pain and exam avg below 60. Slides are premade by another prof and paraphrase the assigned reading, but you cant skip as she quizzes before class. This isnt even a lab. It's pointless and useless.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not a good prof. Reads off slides and makes no sense. Pop quizzes constantly and everything is teamwork.

She is not good at lectures or answering questions, but she changed everyones grade at the end by adding all exercises as extra cred which was her saving grace i guess. A lot of my problems are with the course but also with her lol since I find her aggravating to try and understand.

This woman was literally learning the slides as she reads them and is the most useless prof I've taken. She puts no effort to organize the course on canvas. This course is better self taught than listening to her read off the pre-made slides with her surface level commentary. Unfortunately she was the only prof for the semester.

She's disorganized and is horrible at planning upcoming tests, even when she's told there would be conflicts 2 weeks in advance. The class is not that difficult. The homework is not difficult and is team-focused most of the time. She rushes through example problems in the boring lectures, but she explains the topics decently. Study her test review.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This is gonna cost me a lot of money in therapy.

Dr. Turkan is not an amazing lecturer and you will often be more confused after the lecture than before. Overall, the homework assignments do take a lot of time but they are doable and help to learn the material. She does give plenty of extra credit, and her office hours are very helpful if you are confused on a topic. She is much better at 1 on 1.

She is a nice person, but she will make you want to drop out of the program. She wouldn't pace her lectures so there would be a week with no homework assignments and then assign eight that would take hours each. She wouldn't show up to class and zoom lecture but wouldn't tell the class in advance so everyone would be there. She did give lots of EC.

Dr. Turkan is an overall very kind person, but the class itself is extremely difficult. Assignments are very difficult and are given on a weekly basis with short due dates. But ask to review tests, clarify mistakes and she may offer points. Complete any extra credit, you're going to need it. Exams are exactly like textbook problems. Good luck.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: CHEN is a learning curve in general and she knows it. She is preparing you for the rest of your degree and that is why so many people dislike her. Use excel, buy a calculator with nsolve, and prepare to put in the hours. Has many extra credit opportunities. Had to edit this from earlier bc i actually got an A bc of the extra credit.

There once was a doctor from Turkey
Whose lectures were always quite murky
Much work will be assigned
Do early to avoid a bind
So much extra credit it's quirky

Dr. Turkan was likely the best choice for a intro to CHEN. Everyone below me is just salty that they didn't attend lectures or apply themselves with more effort than an toddler. The lectures were not intuitive in some areas but a good calculator will carry you. I recommend the TI-Inspire CAS CXII calculator. tinyurl com / bddwvdwm. +XtraCred

CHEN is a learning curve in general and she knows it. She is preparing you for the rest of your degree and that is why so many people dislike her. Use excel, buy a calculator with nsolve, prepare to put in the hours, and build a relationship with her and you'll be fine. Has many extra credit opportunities.

She may be a very kind person, but it nowhere near makes up for the horrid teaching style, ridiculous amounts of homework, and awful, unfair exams. This course, and this professor, are both major influences in my change of major, and that of other students who dropped this course with me. Do not take her if at all possible.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The person below is just mad. Dr. Turkan was a great prof. that was constantly looking to improve as a teacher. She also gave many opportunities to improve grades. CHEN 204 definitely has a steep learning curve. However, once you do enough practice and put in the time, like any other class, CHEN 204 becomes relatively easy.

Although there were some hiccups in her first year, Dr. Turkan did a terrific job making sure I understood the material in the foundational class for ChemE. She was always willing to help & constantly looked to improve her teaching for learning. Take her if you want a rock solid foundation for a very tough degree path ahead & not just an easy A.

Throughout the semester, Turkan Aydogmus was pretty abysmal. In the week or so leading up to the final she proved to be astonishingly, remarkably incompetent. She has negative organizational skills, atrocious teaching skills, and is incapable of grading an assignment in less than a month. Not once did she stick to one of her own deadlines.

This is tied with the worst class I have ever taken. The only slightly saving feature of this course was the TAs. Extremely late grading (usually over a month late), ridiculous exams, poor lectures, getting annoyed with us not understanding, the list goes on... Do not take this professor if possible. Good luck in ChemE!
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Aydogmus is really nice and caring but the structure of the course felt truly disorganized, we had to learn material for the exam on the same day the exam was going to be administered. She took over 5 weeks to grade our first exam and most people don't know where they stand in the class because she takes too long with the grading.

Professor Aydogmus is nice, but she is also new and this is reflected very clearly in the class structure. Everything has been so unorganized. The lecture consists of vague, dragged-out examples, while the recitations, homework, and tests contain questions of a much harder caliber. It also took 5 weeks to get the first exam grade in.

Aydogmus is a nice lady, but she has a lot of work to do to improve her teaching skills. Her lectures are miserable to sit through, she does everything last minute, and the class felt very unorganized. Tests were incredibly hard, though she curved pretty well. Homework software she used was super frustrating. Pick a different prof.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She just reads from the power point, and doesn't actually work through a problem and explain what's going on. Once she worked through a problem and even showed us that the book got a different answer, and basically told us they were both right and to do it her way. Asking her questions didn't help either, she just gives vague answers.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Aydogmus' lectures were almost exclusively just reading formulas off of a powerpoint without going over how to apply them. As a result the majority of the class went into the first class unprepared and did very poorly, not accounting for the curve she had to apply. She also grades extremely slow; it took 5 weeks to get grades on our first exam.
